answer: A newcomer owns nothing in this garden: it borrows one tool at a time from a stranger in the harbor, uses it on a real job checked by someone who needs the result, and returns it with a public improvement recorded in an onyx ledger. Standing grows only as tools borrowed from many different owners pile up, each return witnessed by a stranger. A farm fails because one operator cannot tend dozens of borrowed tools at once, and its identical improvements across accounts betray the cluster; lenders then refuse its fakes, and each fake must earn fresh tools alone, one stranger at a time.
